chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said: Abu Ayyub narrated to me from al-Wasafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

In what Allah conversed privately with Musa (peace be upon him) on Mount Thawr, saying: 'O Musa! Inform your people that the nearers do not draw near to Me like those who cry out of fear of Me, and the worshippers do not worship Me like those who are cautious regarding My prohibitions, and the beautifiers do not beautify themselves for Me like those who are ascetic in the world regarding what they are independent of.'
He said: So Musa (peace be upon him) said: 'O the Most Generous of the generous! What have You rewarded them for that?'

He said: 'O Musa! As for those who draw near to Me by crying out of fear of Me, they are in the Highest Companion [or Highest Friend], no one shares with them in it. And as for those who worship Me by being cautious regarding My prohibitions, I examine the people for their deeds, but I do not examine them out of shyness for them. And as for those who draw near to Me by asceticism in the world, I grant them Paradise in its entirety, they take up residence in it wherever they wish.'

key_terms.الرَّفِیقِ الْأَعْلَی: The Highest Companion (referring to God or high rank in Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific ways to draw near to Allah mentioned in this hadith and their corresponding rewards?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, emphasizes that emotional devotion (crying), legal caution (war''), and spiritual detachment (zuhd) are superior forms of worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both inner states and outward adherence to divine law. The unique rewards—proximity to the Highest Companion, exemption from scrutiny, and unrestricted Paradise residence—highlight the multifaceted nature of divine mercy. This narration serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate a balanced spiritual life integrating fear, piety, and asceticism.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Hassan b. Mahbub who said it was narrated to me by Abu Ayoob’ from al-Wasafi from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

“O Musa! There is no one to receive nearness like those among the near ones who cry out of My fear. There is no worshipper like one who worships Me keeping away from what I have prohibited. There is no one who beautifies Me more than those who abstain because they do not beautify themselves with those things they are independent of.”
Musa (a.s.) asked the Lord, “O the Most Merciful of the merciful ones! What is the reward of those people?”

Allah replied, “O Musa! Those who seek nearness fearing Me will be with My best friends where no ordinary person can come. I feel ashamed to inquire about the deeds of those who worship Me keeping away from what I have prohibited. One who seeks nearness to Me through abstinence in this world I will grant him every kind of paradise so that he may live wherever he likes.”
